name: v5-simulacrum-vscode
description: Test VEX V5 robot code without a robot: a simulated V5 brain running VEXos, with its screen, controller, field and motors as panes. Windows (WSL) and macOS.

v5sim.repoPath.markdownDescription: For developers: a clone of the simulator (**v5-simulacrum**, or v5-sim; the folder with `scripts/v5brain.sh`) set up with `scripts/setup.sh`. Empty: a workspace folder that contains one, one next to it, or `~/v5-simulacrum`; without any, the simulator bundled with this extension is used (platform builds of the extension include it). On Windows, the Windows path of the clone.

v5sim.wslDistro.description: On Windows: the WSL distribution the simulator runs in (not used on macOS).

v5sim.preset.markdownDescription: The robot: a preset name from `sim/robots/` (e.g. `competition`, `rw-template`) or a path to any `.args` file.

v5sim.program.description: Optional: a V5 program (.bin) to install in slot v5sim.slot and start once the brain has booted.

v5sim.instanceId.markdownDescription: Simulator instance: `auto` (the first free one) or `0`..`9`. Instance N serves its pages on port 8765+N.

v5sim.extraRobotArgs.markdownDescription: Robot options added to the preset, e.g. `--match 20` or `--physics mujoco`.

v5sim.showBrainWindow.description: Also open QEMU's own brain window (a simulator checkout only; the bundled simulator shows its screen in VS Code).

enumDescriptions: On Windows with usbip-win2 installed, plug the brain into Windows USB (unless one already is); otherwise (and on macOS) serial ports /tmp/ttyV5sys, /tmp/ttyV5user
Always plug the brain into Windows USB through usbip-win2
v5sim.usb.description: How the brain's USB port is exposed, for uploading and the terminal.

v5sim.openBrainOnStart.description: Open the brain screen when a simulator starts.

enumDescriptions: Offer to run each new build on the simulated brain
Run each new build on the simulated brain
v5sim.runOnBuild.markdownDescription: When a build writes a program (VEXcode's `build/*.bin`, PROS's `bin/monolith.bin`): run it on the simulated brain in slot `v5sim.slot`. For a Mac, where VEXcode's Download button can't see the simulator; not on Windows with usbip-win2, where it can.

v5sim.errorReporting.markdownDescription: Send the maintainers a report when the simulator fails to set up or start, or the extension hits an error: the error, where it happened, the extension, VS Code and OS versions, and for a failed start the last lines of the V5 Sim log (home folder and user name taken out). No code. Only sent when VS Code's `#telemetry.telemetryLevel#` allows errors. When it is `all`, each window also sends an active-user session (an anonymous install id and the extension's version) so the maintainers can count users per version; `false` turns that off too.

v5sim.feedbackEndpoint.markdownDescription: Where **V5 Sim: Report a Problem** sends reports (a user setting only: a project's settings can't redirect them). Empty: the report is saved as a zip and a prefilled GitHub issue opens instead.

viewsWelcome.contents:
The VEX V5 brain simulator.
[$(play) Start the simulator](command:v5sim.start)
[Brain screen](command:v5sim.openBrain)
[Device dashboard](command:v5sim.openDashboard)
[Field view](command:v5sim.openField)
[Controller](command:v5sim.openController)
[Configure ports](command:v5sim.configurePorts)
[Run program on sim](command:v5sim.runProgram)
[Stop](command:v5sim.stop)
The first start unpacks the simulator and downloads VEX's firmware (VEXos) from VEX, which takes a few seconds. On Windows the simulator runs in WSL; if it isn't installed, you'll be offered to install it.
[Show log](command:v5sim.showLog) · [Repair simulator](command:v5sim.repair) · [Report a problem](command:v5sim.reportIssue)
